correctness.rationale: On L²(p_n ds), the affine symbol is exactly a^-1 exp(-bs/a)f(s/a). The m-th power yields an exact weighted supremum norm. For b=0 the high-frequency ratio has supremum a^(2nm), inverse power norm a^(m/2), and adjoint eigenvectors t^gamma/p_n(t) span infinite-dimensional kernels throughout the open annulus. For b>0 the normalized supremum converges via compact convergence and uniform exponential tails, and eigenvectors t^gamma exp(-bt/(a-1)) span infinite-dimensional kernels throughout the open disk; both essential spectra follow by closure. The threshold follows from the logarithm inequality, and the b^-n coefficient from uniformly bounded exponential-polynomial rescaling. The norm distance follows from an exact Fourier multiplier formula. All quantifiers n>=1, a>1, b>=0 and endpoints were checked. The standalone finite checker passed but is not an infinite proof.

value.rationale: For a natural recently developed analytic Sobolev operator setting, the theorem identifies a discontinuous spectral transition and a new finite critical-damping parameter governing normalized power growth. It quantifies singular perturbation by a sharp b^-n transient law and an exact nonconvergence-in-norm statement despite strong convergence; Sobolev derivative order is recovered from both the undamped spectral outer radius and the transient exponent. These are motivated structural quantities beyond the qualitative older Zen-space annulus/disk paradigm.
